objective: Create two Android library modules: core-ai and core-speech. core-ai is the ADR-023 containment boundary and the most important module in this scaffold to get right. It is the ONLY module in this repository permitted to name a com.google.mlkit artifact, import an ML Kit type, or declare a @Generable class. It declares both pinned ML Kit dependencies from the catalog -- libs.mlkit.genai.prompt (genai-prompt 1.0.0-beta4) and libs.mlkit.genai.schema.compiler (genai-schema-compiler 1.0.0-alpha1) -- the second applied through ksp(...) since it is a schema-compiling annotation processor. It must expose only plain Kotlin/domain types outward: no ML Kit type may appear in any public signature, so that a breaking change in the alpha library is a single-module repair rather than an app-wide one. core-ai also needs the ProGuard/R8 consumer keep rules ADR-023 requires for schema-compiler-annotated classes: create core-ai/consumer-rules.pro with keep rules covering @Generable-annotated classes and their members, and reference it from the module's build file via defaultConfig.consumerProguardFiles. Kotlin-only sources in core-ai (ADR-023 forbids Java there). core-speech wraps the platform on-device speech recognizer per ADR-024 (android.speech.SpeechRecognizer.createOnDeviceSpeechRecognizer()); in this task it gets only a module scaffold and a capability-detection placeholder -- do NOT implement transcription, and do NOT declare the product's SpeechTranscriber abstraction or any other domain interface. That abstraction is real design owned by a later step, and inventing it here would set a precedent the speech step has to live with. core-speech must declare NO ML Kit dependency: ADR-024 deliberately chose the platform recognizer over com.google.mlkit:genai-speech-recognition, and core-speech is exactly where someone would wrongly reach for it. Both modules: apply ONLY the catalog's android-library alias (plus ksp in core-ai) -- do NOT apply a kotlin-android plugin, which no longer exists in the catalog because AGP 9 has built-in Kotlin support and hard-fails when org.jetbrains.kotlin.android is applied alongside it. Namespaces: com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.ai and com.mcfrenchpants.activityledger.core.speech. Read compileSdk, minSdk and the JDK toolchain from gradle/libs.versions.toml, never as literals. Use minSdkPhone (33) for BOTH modules: core-speech is consumed by the watch too, and a library's minSdk must not exceed its lowest consumer's. Each module gets one clearly-marked scaffold placeholder source file and, where it compiles cleanly, one unit test. core-data/build.gradle.kts and core-testing/build.gradle.kts from SS1.3 are the style reference for an Android library module in this build. THE TWO ML KIT ARTIFACTS HAVE NEVER BEEN RESOLVED FROM A REPOSITORY. genai-schema-compiler is alpha, with no SLA and no deprecation policy. If either fails to resolve, or the schema compiler cannot be applied as a KSP processor, that is a genuine finding about ADR-023's feasibility and must be reported with the exact Gradle error -- do NOT substitute a different version, do NOT drop the dependency silently, and do NOT work around it. Report blocked and stop. Each of these two module directories holds a .gitkeep from SS1.1; delete it once the module has real tracked content, but only in these two modules.
non_goals: Do not implement speech transcription, audio capture, or any recognizer lifecycle.
Do not declare SpeechTranscriber or any other product domain interface, in core-domain or anywhere else -- that is a later step's design decision.
Do not implement prompting, inference, response parsing, or validation logic in core-ai. Placeholders only.
Do not write a real @Generable schema type modelling the interpretation output -- that belongs to the AI vertical-slice backlog item.
Do not add any com.google.mlkit dependency, import or @Generable type to core-speech or to any module other than core-ai.
Do not let any ML Kit type appear in a public signature of core-ai.
Do not touch the other six modules or delete their .gitkeep files.
Do not change any existing version in gradle/libs.versions.toml, and above all do not move Kotlin off 2.3.21.
Do not modify settings.gradle.kts, the root build.gradle.kts, gradle.properties or the Gradle wrapper.
Do not add telemetry, analytics, crash reporting, or any logging of user content -- this is doubly important in core-ai and core-speech, which sit closest to raw user utterances.
Do not add an INTERNET permission or any network code. Nothing in this app goes off device.
Do not edit anything under docs/, .sdlc/, agents/, scripts/, BACKLOG.md, PROGRESS.md, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: `./gradlew :core-ai:assembleDebug :core-speech:assembleDebug` is BUILD SUCCESSFUL. State the evidence, not just the exit code.

Both ML Kit artifacts actually resolved from a repository: report the resolved coordinates for com.google.mlkit:genai-prompt:1.0.0-beta4 and com.google.mlkit:genai-schema-compiler:1.0.0-alpha1 as they appear in `./gradlew :core-ai:dependencies`. If either did not resolve, the task is blocked, not done.

ADR-023 containment holds repo-wide: core-ai is the ONLY module whose build file names a com.google.mlkit coordinate, and no source file outside core-ai imports an ML Kit type or declares a @Generable class. Verify by grepping every *.gradle.kts and every *.kt in the repo (excluding build output) and state the result.
No ML Kit type appears in any public signature of core-ai -- scaffold types are internal or expose only plain Kotlin/domain types. State how this was checked.

core-ai/consumer-rules.pro exists, contains keep rules for schema-compiler-annotated (@Generable) classes and their members, and is referenced from core-ai's build file via consumerProguardFiles. Show the referencing line.
core-speech declares no ML Kit dependency and no product domain interface (no SpeechTranscriber or equivalent).
Neither module applies a kotlin-android plugin, and gradle/libs.versions.toml is byte-for-byte unchanged (`git diff -- gradle/libs.versions.toml` empty).
Both modules read compileSdk, minSdk and the JDK toolchain from the catalog; the literals 36, 33 and 21 do not appear in either build file. Both use minSdkPhone.
Neither module declares an INTERNET permission, contains network code, or logs user content.
Every placeholder source file is clearly marked in comments as a scaffold placeholder with no product meaning.
